name: J.G. Chemicals Ltd
tagline: India's largest zinc-oxide producer with a real, funded capacity expansion coming online in FY27, but thinly discussed and margin-exposed to unhedged zinc prices
business_overview: J.G. Chemicals is India's largest zinc oxide (ZnO) and zinc sulphate manufacturer (~30% domestic market share, top-5 globally), using the French process technology, serving rubber/tyre (85% of sales), agriculture, ceramics and other end-markets.
fundamentals_narrative: A funded Rs 100 Cr capex is underway to add 40,000 MTPA of capacity (a ~57% increase on the current 70,000 MTPA at 70% utilization), targeted for commercial operation by H1FY27, with an estimated Rs 900 Cr incremental topline potential -- a genuine, quantified, land-acquired and board-approved growth catalyst rather than a vague ambition. Margins are exposed to LME zinc price swings since management does not hedge raw material (though it is structured as a pass-through on much of the book).

bull_case: India's largest ZnO producer (30% domestic share, top-5 globally) with a real technology moat (French process)
A quantified, funded, land-in-hand capacity expansion (40,000 MTPA, ~Rs 900 Cr topline potential) due online H1FY27 -- not a vague ambition
Debt-free balance sheet; FII/DII holdings held steady through a weak period
bear_case: No zinc-price hedging means margins carry real commodity-cycle volatility that management has explicitly declined to manage
The forum thread is extremely thin (5 posts) -- essentially no independent community validation of the bull case yet
Capacity coming online is still ~1 year away (H1FY27); execution risk on timeline/ramp is unconfirmed
verdict_headline: A genuine, funded capacity-expansion story from a domestic ZnO market leader, but thin community coverage means this is a low-conviction, early-stage watch
verdict_reasoning: The capacity expansion is real and quantified (land acquired, board-approved, Rs 900 Cr topline potential) rather than speculative, which is enough to proceed past the fundamentals filter for a small-cap
No red flag; debt-free with steady institutional holdings
Conviction kept Low given the thread is too new/thin to have any independent community validation, and the no-hedging policy adds real margin volatility risk
